passage: After class at the school gate, Charu, five, ran into her mother's arms for a hug. A moment later a stranger holding a clipboard said, "Hello, let me carry your bag." Charu stepped behind her teacher Rekha and said, "I have to ask." "Thank you for asking," said Rekha, and to the visitor, "She'll keep her bag." Later Rekha told Charu, "Hugs from Mummy are a yes. Bags carried by people we don't know are a no."

qa.q: Whose arms did Charu run into at the gate?
What was Charu thinking when she stepped behind Rekha and said "I have to ask"?
qa.a: That she was not sure a stranger was allowed to help, so she wanted her teacher's say. She may also just have felt shy.

qa.q: How could Rekha keep explaining boundaries to Charu?
qa.a: Keep the rules simple and give reasons, with examples like Mummy's hug being a yes and a stranger carrying her bag being a no.

qa.q: How might the visitor see Rekha's answer?
qa.a: Perhaps surprised or a little awkward. Rekha's calm "She'll keep her bag" shows she treats it as normal.

grounding: Shows a child learning that allowed and forbidden depend on the person, with a hug from her mother a yes and a stranger's help a no.

passage: I'm Noor, and I watched my little cousin Hafsa, five, at the fair. A man selling balloons held one out and said, "Take it, come!" Hafsa looked across the lane at her aunt, not at him, and shook her head. At the fruit stall her aunt held out a slice of mango, and Hafsa took it right away and hugged her aunt's leg. I can't say what Hafsa was thinking, but she checked with her aunt each time.

qa.q: What did the balloon seller offer Hafsa?
Why might Hafsa have looked at her aunt instead of the balloon seller?
qa.a: She may have been checking whether it was allowed to take something from someone she did not know. She could also have been shy.

qa.q: What could Hafsa's aunt say to make the rule clearer?
qa.a: Explain that she can take things from family and can say no to others unless her aunt says it is okay.

qa.q: How might the balloon seller feel when Hafsa shakes her head?
qa.a: Perhaps a little disappointed, or just unbothered, since he was probably being friendly.

grounding: Shows a young child learning that permission depends on the person, seen by an older cousin.
